subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 34-year-old man of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry is evaluated for fatigue and early satiety. He has had two episodes of severe left hip pain that were treated as bone crises. Examination shows massive splenomegaly and scattered petechiae. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, platelets 68,000/µL, and an elevated serum acid phosphatase. Bone marrow biopsy reveals large lipid-laden macrophages with a fibrillary, crumpled tissue paper appearance.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Gaucher disease is the most common lysosomal storage disease and results from deficient glucocerebrosidase, with glucocerebroside accumulating in cells of the monocyte-macrophage lineage. The clinical picture includes hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, osteoporosis, avascular necrosis of the femoral head, and bone crises. The characteristic Gaucher cells are lipid-laden macrophages that resemble crumpled tissue paper, and treatment with recombinant glucocerebrosidase is available.

explanation_incorrect.B: Sphingomyelinase deficiency causes Niemann-Pick disease, in which the marrow shows foam cells and a cherry-red macular spot is typical.
explanation_incorrect.C: Galactocerebrosidase deficiency causes Krabbe disease, with globoid cells in white matter and peripheral demyelination rather than bone crises and splenomegaly.
explanation_incorrect.D: α-L-Iduronidase deficiency causes Hurler syndrome, which presents in infancy with coarse facial features, corneal clouding, and skeletal deformities.
explanation_incorrect.E: Iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency causes Hunter syndrome, an X-linked disorder with coarse features and aggressive behavior.

educationalObjective: Hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, bone crises, and crumpled tissue paper macrophages in an adult indicate Gaucher disease, caused by glucocerebrosidase deficiency and treated with enzyme replacement.
